correctness.independent_verification: Independent implementation of quiver unit multiplication, direct centralizer counting and graph support formula for three distinct small quivers at q=2,3 gives identical conjugacy-class size distributions. Independently summed the exact support formula for the two six-vertex examples, recovering the SAME class number 2340 and size-three class counts 2 versus 0. This checks the claimed distinction, not just group order. Source checker.py inspected, not executed as proof; all-quiver theorem follows from explicitly checked orbit-stabilizer/centralizer algebra.
correctness.rationale: For arbitrary finite quiver with loops and parallel/opposite arrows, the algebra is D⊕J with J²=0 and units (t,x) with (t,x)(s,y)=(ts,ty+xs). Radical conjugation uniquely kills arrow coordinates on nonmonochromatic edges (t_u≠t_v), while monochromatic blocks survive. A support F of nonzero monochromatic bundles forces diagonal stabilizer equality along F, so its torus orbit size is (q−1)^(n−c(F)) and orbit count is (q−1)^beta(F) times product (q^mu_e−1)/(q−1). The full centralizer equation also yields the class size q^mu(E\B(t)) (q−1)^(n−c(F)), with q^h central loop factor; summing over t and F proves the exact stated class-size polynomial. For q>2 coprime q,(q−1) give singleton and size-q coefficients, with the size-q coefficient measuring multiplicity-one bridges. For q=2 the group is abelian and the bridge conclusion is correctly excluded. Arbitrary disconnected graphs and oppositely directed bundles are covered.

value.rationale: Determines EVERY conjugacy-class size coefficient for an arbitrary finite quiver unit group, significantly refining previously known total class numbers. The multiplicity-one bridge invariant is recovered from the lowest coefficients, and a concrete equal-order/equal-class-number pair is separated by sizes. Such group invariants are natural for representation-theoretic and combinatorial classification, not an arbitrary small parameter count.
